q: In Hindu tradition, the Sanskrit epic Ramayana is traditionally attributed to which sage?
e: Valmiki is traditionally credited with the Sanskrit Ramayana. Tulsidas later wrote the Awadhi retelling, Ramcharitmanas.

q: In the Mahabharata, who delivers the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna?
e: The Bhagavad Gita is a dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra.

q: Which deity in Hindu tradition is depicted with the head of an elephant?
e: Ganesha, son of Shiva and Parvati, is depicted with an elephant head and is revered as the remover of obstacles.

q: In Hindu tradition, which divine bird serves as the mount (vahana) of Vishnu?
e: Garuda is Vishnu's vahana. Nandi is Shiva's bull, Airavata is Indra's elephant and Mushika is Ganesha's mouse.

q: In the Mahabharata, which Pandava brother was famed for his immense strength and his skill with the mace?
e: Bhima, the second Pandava, was renowned for his strength and fought with a mace (gada).

q: According to Puranic accounts of the Samudra Manthana (churning of the ocean), which serpent was used as the churning rope?
e: The serpent king Vasuki was wound around Mount Mandara, which served as the churning rod.

q: In the Mahabharata, who narrates the events of the Kurukshetra war to the blind king Dhritarashtra?
e: Sanjaya, granted divine sight by Vyasa, describes the war to Dhritarashtra.

q: In the Ramayana, which brother of Ravana left Lanka and joined Rama's side?
e: Vibhishana counselled Ravana to return Sita, was rejected, and allied with Rama. Indrajit was Ravana's son.

q: In Puranic Hindu cosmology, which of the four yugas is described as the current age?
e: The Puranas describe a cycle of Satya, Treta, Dvapara and Kali yugas, with the present age being Kali Yuga.

q: In Greek mythology, who is the king of the gods, ruling from Mount Olympus?
e: Zeus rules Olympus; his brothers Poseidon and Hades rule the sea and the underworld.

q: In Norse mythology, what is the name of Thor's hammer?
e: Thor wields Mjölnir. Gungnir is Odin's spear and Draupnir is Odin's ring.

q: In ancient Egyptian religion, which jackal-headed god is associated with mummification and the afterlife?
e: Anubis oversaw embalming and guided souls. Horus is falcon-headed and Thoth is usually ibis-headed.

q: In Greek mythology, who flew too close to the sun on wings of feathers and wax?
e: Icarus ignored his father Daedalus' warning; the wax melted and he fell into the sea.

q: In Norse mythology, what is the name of the immense world tree that connects the nine worlds?
e: Yggdrasil is the cosmic ash tree. Bifröst is the rainbow bridge to Asgard.

q: In Roman mythology, which god corresponds to the Greek god of war, Ares?
e: Mars is the Roman counterpart of Ares; Mercury corresponds to Hermes, Jupiter to Zeus and Vulcan to Hephaestus.

q: In Japanese Shinto mythology, which sun goddess hid in a cave, plunging the world into darkness?
e: Amaterasu retreated into the Ama-no-Iwato cave after conflict with her brother Susanoo. Tsukuyomi is the moon god.

q: In the Mesopotamian Epic of Gilgamesh, Gilgamesh is the king of which city?
e: Gilgamesh is the legendary king of Uruk who seeks immortality after the death of his companion Enkidu.

q: How many days are there in a leap year?
e: A leap year adds 29 February, giving 366 days.

q: Which colour is produced by mixing blue and yellow paint?
e: In subtractive (paint) colour mixing, blue and yellow make green.

q: What is the official currency of Japan?
e: Japan uses the yen. The won is Korean, the yuan Chinese and the ringgit Malaysian.

q: Which organ in the human body produces the hormone insulin?
e: Beta cells in the pancreatic islets of Langerhans produce insulin.

q: Which naturally occurring material is the hardest on the Mohs scale?
e: Diamond ranks 10 on the Mohs hardness scale, the maximum.

q: In which city is the ancient Colosseum located?
e: The Flavian Amphitheatre, known as the Colosseum, stands in the centre of Rome.

q: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
e: A standard modern piano has 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.

q: How many bones does a typical adult human skeleton have?
e: The typical adult skeleton has 206 bones; infants have more, which fuse during growth.

q: Which gas do plants mainly absorb from the air for photosynthesis?
e: Plants take in carbon dioxide and, using light energy, produce glucose and release oxygen.

q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
e: Au comes from the Latin 'aurum'. Ag is silver and Gd is gadolinium.

q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
e: Iron oxide on its surface gives Mars its reddish appearance.

q: In eukaryotic cells, which structure contains most of the cell's genetic material?
e: The nucleus houses chromosomal DNA. Mitochondria hold a small amount of their own DNA.

q: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
e: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω); volts measure potential difference, amperes current, watts power.

q: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
e: Light travels at exactly 299,792,458 m/s in a vacuum, roughly 300,000 km/s.

q: Which element has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale?
e: Fluorine has a Pauling electronegativity of about 3.98, the highest of all elements.

q: Absolute zero (0 kelvin) is equal to which temperature in degrees Celsius?
e: 0 K is defined as −273.15 °C. −459.67 is the Fahrenheit value.

q: What does CPU stand for?
e: The CPU is the Central Processing Unit that executes program instructions.

q: What does HTML stand for?
e: HTML, HyperText Markup Language, structures content on the web.

q: How many bits make up one byte?
e: In modern computing a byte is 8 bits.

q: Which programming language was created by Guido van Rossum?
e: Guido van Rossum released Python in 1991. Ruby is by Yukihiro Matsumoto, Java by James Gosling, Perl by Larry Wall.

q: Which data structure follows the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) principle?
e: A stack removes the most recently added item first. A queue is First-In, First-Out.

q: What is the default TCP port for HTTPS?
e: HTTPS uses port 443 by default; plain HTTP uses 80 and FTP uses 21.

q: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
e: Binary search halves the search space every step, taking O(log n) comparisons.

q: Who wrote what is widely regarded as the first published algorithm intended for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine?
e: In 1843 Ada Lovelace published notes including an algorithm to compute Bernoulli numbers on the Analytical Engine.

q: In networking, what does DNS primarily do?
a: Translates domain names into IP addresses
e: The Domain Name System resolves human-readable names like example.com to IP addresses.

q: In which year did World War II end?
e: The war ended in 1945: in Europe in May and in Asia with Japan's surrender in August/September.

q: Who was the first President of the United States?
e: George Washington served as the first President from 1789 to 1797.

q: In which year did India gain independence from British rule?
e: India became independent on 15 August 1947. It became a republic in 1950.

q: Which civilisation built the citadel of Machu Picchu?
e: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 15th century in the Andes of present-day Peru.

q: Who founded the Maurya Empire in ancient India?
e: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire around 322 BCE; Ashoka was his grandson.

q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
e: The Berlin Wall was opened on 9 November 1989. It had been built in 1961.

q: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between the British East India Company and which ruler?
e: Robert Clive's forces defeated Siraj ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, aided by the defection of Mir Jafar.

q: Which treaty, signed in 1919, formally ended World War I between the Allied Powers and Germany?
e: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919. Westphalia (1648) ended the Thirty Years' War.

q: What is the capital city of Australia?
e: Canberra was purpose-built as the capital as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
e: The Pacific covers roughly a third of Earth's surface.

q: Which river flows through Cairo?
e: Cairo lies on the banks of the Nile, just south of the Nile Delta.

q: Mount Everest lies on the border between Nepal and which country?
e: Everest's summit sits on the border of Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.

q: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
e: The Sahara is the largest hot desert. Antarctica is the largest desert overall (a cold desert).

q: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
e: Vatican City covers about 0.44 km², making it the smallest sovereign state.

q: Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake, is located in which country?
e: Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, is over 1,600 m deep.

q: Which strait separates Asia from North America?
e: The Bering Strait lies between Russia's Chukotka Peninsula and Alaska.

q: How many players from one team are on the field at a time in association football (soccer)?
e: Each side fields 11 players, including the goalkeeper.

q: In which sport is a score of zero called "love"?
e: Tennis uses 'love' for zero, as in 'fifteen-love'.

q: How many interlocking rings appear on the Olympic flag?
e: The five rings represent the union of the five inhabited continents as conceived in the Olympic movement.

q: Which country won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
e: Hosts Uruguay beat Argentina 4–2 in the 1930 final in Montevideo.

q: How many legal deliveries make up a standard over in cricket?
e: A standard over consists of six legal deliveries.

q: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
e: The 1896 Games in Athens were the first of the modern Olympic era.

q: Who was the first batter to score a double century in a men's One Day International?
e: Tendulkar scored 200* against South Africa in Gwalior in February 2010. Belinda Clark had made the first women's ODI 200 in 1997.

q: What is the official distance of a marathon?
e: The marathon distance was standardised at 42.195 km (26 miles 385 yards) in 1921.

q: Who directed the 1993 film "Jurassic Park"?
e: Steven Spielberg directed Jurassic Park, based on Michael Crichton's novel.

q: In Disney's "The Lion King" (1994), what is the name of Simba's father?
e: Mufasa is Simba's father; Scar is his uncle.

q: In the 1975 Hindi film "Sholay", what is the name of the infamous dacoit villain?
e: Gabbar Singh, played by Amjad Khan, is the villain of Sholay. Mogambo is from Mr. India (1987).

q: Who composed the score for the original "Star Wars" (1977)?
e: John Williams composed the Star Wars score, which won the Academy Award for Best Original Score.

q: James Cameron's 2009 film "Avatar" is set on which fictional moon?
e: Avatar takes place on Pandora. Endor is from Star Wars, Arrakis from Dune and LV-426 from Alien.

q: Which film became the first non-English-language winner of the Academy Award for Best Picture (2020 ceremony)?
e: Bong Joon-ho's South Korean film Parasite won Best Picture at the 92nd Academy Awards in February 2020.

q: Which song from the film "RRR" won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 2023?
e: 'Naatu Naatu', composed by M. M. Keeravani, won in March 2023. 'Jai Ho' won in 2009 for Slumdog Millionaire.

q: Who directed the 1954 Japanese film "Seven Samurai"?
e: Akira Kurosawa directed Seven Samurai, one of the most influential films ever made.

q: In "Naruto", which hidden village is Naruto Uzumaki from?
e: Naruto is a ninja of Konohagakure, the Village Hidden in the Leaves.

q: In "One Piece", what is the name of Monkey D. Luffy's crew?
e: Luffy captains the Straw Hat Pirates, named after his signature straw hat.

q: Which animation studio produced "Spirited Away" (2001)?
e: Spirited Away was directed by Hayao Miyazaki at Studio Ghibli and won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

q: In "Dragon Ball", what is Goku's Saiyan birth name?
e: Goku was born Kakarot. Raditz is his brother and Bardock his father.

q: In "Attack on Titan", which is the outermost of the three main walls protecting humanity?
e: From outermost to innermost the walls are Maria, Rose and Sina.

q: In "Death Note", which Shinigami drops the Death Note into the human world?
e: Ryuk drops his notebook out of boredom, and Light Yagami finds it.

q: In "Demon Slayer", which breathing style does Tanjiro first learn from Sakonji Urokodaki?
e: Urokodaki trains Tanjiro in Water Breathing; he later also uses Sun Breathing (Hinokami Kagura).

q: In "Fullmetal Alchemist", what is the fundamental law of alchemy called?
e: Equivalent Exchange states that to obtain something, something of equal value must be lost.

q: Who created the "Dragon Ball" manga?
e: Akira Toriyama created Dragon Ball. Oda created One Piece, Kishimoto Naruto and Kubo Bleach.

q: Who wrote the play "Romeo and Juliet"?
e: Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet in the mid-1590s.

q: Who wrote the "Harry Potter" book series?
e: J. K. Rowling wrote the seven Harry Potter novels (1997–2007).

q: Who received the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature, notably for the English "Gitanjali"?
e: Tagore was the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

q: Which novel opens with the line "Call me Ishmael."?
w: The Old Man and the Sea
e: Herman Melville's Moby-Dick (1851) begins with 'Call me Ishmael.'

q: Who wrote the dystopian novel "Nineteen Eighty-Four"?
e: George Orwell published Nineteen Eighty-Four in 1949. Huxley wrote Brave New World.

q: Who wrote "One Hundred Years of Solitude"?
e: García Márquez published the novel in 1967; it is a landmark of magical realism.

q: In which language did Kalidasa compose "Abhijnanashakuntalam"?
e: Kalidasa wrote the play in Sanskrit (with some characters speaking Prakrit, as was dramatic convention).

q: Who wrote the epic poem "Paradise Lost"?
e: John Milton published Paradise Lost in 1667.

q: Which country hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi in September 2023?
e: India held the G20 presidency in 2023 and hosted the summit on 9–10 September 2023.

q: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
e: Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee. Rajendra Prasad presided over the Constituent Assembly.

q: Which city hosted the 2024 Summer Olympic Games?
e: Paris hosted the Games from 26 July to 11 August 2024. Los Angeles is scheduled for 2028.

q: In August 2023, which country's Chandrayaan-3 mission made the first soft landing near the Moon's south pole?
e: ISRO's Vikram lander touched down on 23 August 2023. Russia's Luna-25 crashed days earlier.

q: How many permanent members does the United Nations Security Council have?
e: China, France, Russia, the UK and the US are the five permanent members; there are 15 members in total.

q: Which union did the United Kingdom formally leave on 31 January 2020?
e: Brexit took legal effect on 31 January 2020, followed by a transition period to 31 December 2020.

q: Which organisation was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 at the September 2023 New Delhi summit?
e: The African Union joined as a permanent member in September 2023; the European Union was already a member.

q: Which country became NATO's 31st member in April 2023?
e: Finland joined on 4 April 2023. Sweden followed as the 32nd member in March 2024.

q: On which date did the Constitution of India come into effect?
e: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).

q: What is 12 × 12?
e: 12 × 12 = 144, also called a gross.

q: What is the value of π rounded to two decimal places?
e: π ≈ 3.14159…, which rounds to 3.14.

q: What is 15% of 200?
What is the square root of 169?
What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle in Euclidean geometry?
e: In Euclidean geometry the interior angles of any triangle add up to 180°.

q: What is the smallest prime number greater than 13?
e: 14, 15 and 16 are composite; 17 is prime.

q: What is 7! (7 factorial)?
What is the derivative of sin(x) with respect to x?
e: d/dx sin(x) = cos(x).

q: How many diagonals does a convex hexagon have?
e: An n-sided polygon has n(n−3)/2 diagonals: 6 × 3 / 2 = 9.
